title: Need Help
author: lonewolf172276
selftext:
So for the last year I have been trying to learn trading. I keep having people offer to help teach me and while I am learning I can copy trade what they do. I have been scammed 3 times already and currently feel like I am being scammed again. Needless to say, I am done trusting anyone at this point. 

So I have been hearing a lot about AI trading bots, or let AI trade for you. I have heard good and bad things about this, mostly bad. I am over $15k in the hole due to these scams and I am done with the BS.

Please give me your opinions on AI trading bots or good, honest platforms that can help.

comments.author: thepromptgenius
comments.body:
any platform that promises a "bot" that can trade for you i'd steer away from, even in the off chance that a profitable bot does exist, edge decay will hit it as soon as it's made public which is why nobody in their right mind would publish a profitable bot with real long term edge. a bot can make a couple of profitable trades (even a coin flip is profitable 50% of the time) before the draw down hits so avoid it

there's no shortcut unfortunately, you need to learn how to trade yourself. AI can help in the sense you can ask questions it can answer, it can help you backtest, verify your strategies, explore, etc, but not trade on your behalf, it's a copilot not a pilot.

comments.author: Routine_Bat6675
comments.body: Any tool that promise you easy gains is a fraud, the only thing that works for me is actually analyzing stocks, i personally use mainly [Sentimentick.com](http://Sentimentick.com) for that, it doesn't trade for me but it gives me useful insights because they analyze the stocks for me.

comments.author: Smart-Ride-7047
comments.body:
I spent 4+ years learning first, then trying to build a robust trading system. Got shitload of experience, but no financial gains (no losses as welll, tho, besides operational cost). Maybe I am stupid, maybe just kept walking into the wrong direction, until life made me stop.

Don’t ever put your money into black boxes. Even the prettiest of them all equity curve might have been 1 step away from catastrophic unrealized risk.

comments.author: Good_Character_20
comments.body: Sorry you got hit that hard. Notice that all three scams ran on the same hook, someone else making money for you, and let AI trade for you is that same hook in a new outfit. Bots marketed that way, especially anything promising returns or asking you to fund their platform, are mostly aimed at people who are tired and want it handled for them. The honest version of automation never touches your money. It's you testing your own rules on a brokerage account you opened yourself, where nobody else has access and there is nobody to send funds to. The moment a person or platform offers to trade on your behalf or quotes you a return, it's the same thing that already cost you 15k. Start on a paper account with fake money until you can see an approach work with your own eyes. It's slow and boring, which is the opposite of how the scams feel.

comments.author: BluFinTun_Dwa
comments.body:
Maybe start with a "bot like" trading approach? 
Find a interesting stock, check if you can trade it at your broker. 
And then discuss the pros/cons with an AI-chatbot of your choice? 

You also learn more because the chatbot will explain it.

comments.author: CryptonianNomad
comments.body:
Don't pay to learn... You start by developing your own strategy and build on that. 

What I recommend religiously on here is keep things simple because trading is very difficult. 

My strategy doesn't get anymore simple and here it is: 

1. Daily chart - use this for trend direction. 
2. 4hr chart - use to mark up areas of support land resistance. 
3. 1 HR chart - use this for your entry. Your stop should be above or below the previous swing high or swing low. (Give it some wiggle room)
4. Rsi - use the rsi for identify bearish or bullish divergence. This will add confluence to your idea. 
5. Leave all emotions at home and don't allow them to get involved in your trading. 
6. Aim for a realistic 1:2rr and risk no more than 2% per trade or 2% over all trades you enter and have open at any one time. 

If all charts align then you have a good set up. 

Once you master this and see results then you can run with it and start building on top of a very simple and profitable strategy. 

Good luck 👍
